title: Zero passphrase and stdin read buffers; tighten the hidden-read zeroing test (WCLI-136 opus follow-up)
description: Follow-up from the opus APPROVE at f23c619 of ward-cli#256 (WCLI-136): secret-buffer hygiene beyond the hidden prompt, pre-existing and out of #256's scope. readPassphraseBytes (src/adapters/passphrase.ts) never zeroes its bytes or buffer on any path, backup_passphrase_too_large and Ctrl-C included, and calls readSync directly with no EAGAIN or EINTR retry (readOnce has one). readStdinValueBytes (src/adapters/secret-value.ts) never zeroes its chunk buffers or its number[]. Two small items from the same review: the test 'a refused read zeroes what it read, and so does a read that returns' must assert the expected bytes.length on all four cases (an every() over an empty array is vacuously true, so bytes.length = 0 would pass the token and abandoned cases), and the readHiddenValueBytes doc comment should say 'the bytes still held' because fill(0) cannot reach a byte already removed by backspace pop or an old backing store.

acceptanceCriteria.text: readPassphraseBytes zeroes its bytes and buffer on every way out, including backup_passphrase_too_large and Ctrl-C, retries EAGAIN and EINTR as readOnce does, and a test fails when each zeroing is removed
readStdinValueBytes zeroes its chunk buffers and its number[] on every way out, and a test fails when that zeroing is removed
The hidden-read zeroing test asserts the expected bytes.length on all four cases, and the doc comment says the bytes still held
